title: Sakchi becomes Jamshedpur
body: Sakchi was once a small village on the Chota Nagpur Plateau. It was chosen as the site of Asia's first steel plant because it lay close to rich deposits of iron ore. The Tata family wanted to build a township with modern facilities for everyone working in the factory, and Sir Dorabji Tata even built a hospital in the village before steel production began. The town was designed with wide, tree-lined streets, gardens, open spaces, houses and civic amenities. In 1919 Sakchi was renamed Jamshedpur. Because of its planned development, more factories came up in the region, and people from within and outside the state moved there for work. Today it is the largest industrial city in Jharkhand.

title: Reviving the lakes of Bengaluru
body: Bengaluru, a modern metropolis, faces water shortages in summer and flooding during the monsoon. Overuse of groundwater, a lack of rainwater harvesting and the encroachment of lake beds have made the problem worse. The city once had about 1,000 lakes, but rapid urbanisation reduced them to about 200, and many of those were polluted by sewage and chemicals. Wells dried up. Some lakes, such as Bellandur and Varthur, were covered in foam, released toxic gases and even caught fire. Non-profit organisations, Resident Welfare Associations (RWAs) and local communities have begun reviving lakes by desilting them, repairing bunds with natural materials, clearing drainage channels, planting native species and restocking fish. Such work can increase the water available to residents and restore the ecological balance of the surrounding area.
